Tom - great to chat yesterday. Appreciate the clear usage signal. Below is a concise unit-econ sketch plus next steps; I attached a token estimate workbook for the volumes you gave (FintechX_token_estimates.xlsx).

Quick answers up-front:
- Target price bands we typically model (hosted API): $150- $450 per 1M prompt+completion tokens depending on model family, latency SLO, and commitment level. For a pilot with bursty traffic and no long-term commit, expect mid-to-upper band. With a 12-mo Reserved capacity commit we can reach low band.
- Inference cost-to-Retail margin (illustrative):
  - Inference cost (Redwood internal): $30- $80 per 1M tokens (varies by GPU, batch efficiency, KV cache hit rate, quantization).
  - Suggested gross margin target for product: 50-65% -> implies target retail price of ~$60- $160 per 1M tokens if you want 50-65% margin on top of the raw inference cost.

Unit-econ sketch (using your numbers):
- Assumptions: 1.8M calls/day peak, avg 800 tokens/call -> ~1.44B tokens/day peak -> ~43.2B tokens/month peak.
- Pilot sizing (expected initial ramp): 10% of peak -> ~4.32B tokens/month.
- Pricing examples (hosted, pay-as-you-go):
  - If priced at $250 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost = $250 * 4,320 = $1,080,000 (pilot).
  - If priced at $150 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost = $648,000.
- Inference unit cost (Redwood internal estimate):
  - Baseline (fp16, standard batching) ~$70 / 1M tokens.
  - Optimized (int8/quant, aggressive batching, caching): ~$30- $45 / 1M tokens.

$/feature & margin math (example):
- Feature: personalized micro-recommendation per user session (assume 1 call/session). At peak 1.8M calls/day -> feature cost per session at $70/1M tokens = $0.00007 * 800 tokens = $0.056 per session.
- If you price the feature as an embedded value (e.g., convert to revenue per user):
  - Revenue per session required for 50% gross margin = $0.112/session.
  - CAC payback: if CAC = $10/user and ARPU uplift from the feature = $0.20/month, payback ~50 months (not viable) -> you need either lower CAC, larger uplift, or amortize across other features.

Practical recommendation for pilot given your procurement budget ($20k- $50k/mo):
- Pilot approach: 1) narrow sample cohort (1-5% of traffic) to get production signal; 2) use a smaller model variant with aggressive quantization and prefix caching; 3) enable our batching & KV caching to reduce token compute. Expected pilot cost estimate: with 1% traffic (~432M tokens/mo) and price at $150/1M -> ~$64.8k/mo (still above $50k). With deeper opt (choose int8 model + reserved burst windows) could be $20k- $35k/mo. Attached workbook shows permutations.

Next steps
1) I attached FintechX_token_estimates.xlsx with a few scenarios. Please review and confirm which ramp scenario you want to model.
2) Rishi (cc'd) can run an internal perf check to validate achievable token cost for the model family you prefer.
3) If pilot budget is constrained, we can propose a scoped technical pilot (smaller cohort, higher sampling) or a 3-month commit to hit reserved pricing.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call - I have slots Tue/Wed 10-12 PT next week. Which works for you?

Best,

Adding a couple implementation notes from infra/SE perspective that will materially affect the inference $/1M tokens: 

- Model/quantization: moving to int8 or bfloat16 mixed path reduces per-token compute ~2x-3x on supported GPUs. If FintechX is comfortable trading some latency/quality we can aim for $30- $45 / 1M tokens.
- Batching and prefix caching: if your traffic pattern is suitable (many repeat prefixes, same user segments), KV cache hit rates can reduce compute by additional 20-40%.
- Throughput optimizations: recommend starting pilot on dedicated capacity for a predictable 95th pct latency. Dedicated pools + short-term reserved capacity will lower unit cost vs pure hosted burst.
- Ops: we can instrument token-level cost, per-route latency, and a daily estimated spend dashboard for procurement.

I'll attach our standard pricing & commitment options for quick reference (Redwood_pricing_options.pdf). If you want, I can run a quick perf run against a small sample model with sample prompt traces to produce a tighter cost number (2-3 day turn).

--Rishi
